{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ee2fa4642880c15b6dae79f3da1fb464f3ba82d6624fbbe9c9848f35a41917f4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving conditions: bald tires, reduced visibility, severe weather, hydroplaning and skids, winter driving and rural farm hazards","heading":"C — Driving conditions: planning for hazards, bald tires, fog and night visibility, slippery and icy roads, hydroplaning and skid recovery, winter driving and snowplows, and farm equipment and livestock on rural roads","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driving conditions: planning for hazards, bald tires, fog and night visibility, slippery and icy roads, hydroplaning and skid recovery, winter driving and snowplows, and farm equipment and livestock on rural roads
Knowledge domain: adjusting to conditions that make driving harder — poor visibility, slick or icy pavement, Wisconsin winters and rural farm traffic — and recovering safely from hydroplaning and skids.

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Plan ahead and check your vehicle before you leave, and stay home when the roads look icy or unsafe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Heavily worn tires are called bald tires, and they lower traction and lengthen stopping distance, which is especially dangerous in bad weather. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
When visibility is reduced, other vehicles can seem to move slower than they really are. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
At night it is harder to judge how far away oncoming vehicles are and how fast they are going. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
In fog, rain or other low-visibility conditions, slow down, be ready to stop and use your headlights to see better. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
When roads are slippery, icy, snow covered or flooded with heavy rain, the best choice is to stay off the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
In severe weather, bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
If you must drive on slick roads, slow down, stay alert and avoid hard braking or sudden sharp turns so you keep control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
In a car without an anti-lock braking system, gently pump the brakes to help keep it from skidding or sliding on slippery roads. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Watch for slippery or icy pavement in shady spots and on bridges and overpasses on cold, wet days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
Roads are also likely to be slippery when the temperature is near freezing, when rain first begins to fall, and where water stands near the shoulder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
Hydroplaning means your tires are riding on top of water instead of the road, and with bald tires it can happen even at low speeds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
If you begin to hydroplane, ease off the gas, keep the steering wheel straight, and do not brake or turn until the tires grip the road again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
The handbook describes a skid as your tires bouncing on the road after you have lost control of the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
In a skid, stay off the brake and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
As soon as the car starts to straighten out of a skid, turn the wheel back the other way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Be extra alert on the first day of snowfall, because people are not yet used to driving in snow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Before a winter drive, clear snow and ice from the whole vehicle, including every window, the lights, the side mirrors and the license plates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
In winter, drive slowly and leave extra space ahead of your vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Do not use cruise control on slippery roads. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
In winter conditions, turn on your headlights but do not use your high beams. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
Stay at least 200 feet back from a snowplow whose lights are flashing red, amber or green. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A02
Rural roads bring special hazards such as slow tractors, farm equipment and livestock. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A02
Farmers may have trouble seeing or hearing other traffic, and their equipment may have no brake lights or turn signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A02
Be patient around farm equipment on the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A02
You must yield the right-of-way to livestock on or beside the highway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A02
Near livestock, do not honk, since it may frighten the animals; slow down and keep a safe distance instead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A02
No one younger than 16 may drive a farm tractor or self-propelled farm machinery on a highway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

Misconceptions: slower-looking traffic in fog may actually be moving faster than it seems; a bridge can be icy even when the road leading to it is not; hydroplaning is not only a high-speed problem when tires are bald; braking hard in a skid makes things worse, so stay off the brake; winter driving means headlights on but brights off; honking at livestock may scare them.
Mnemonics: bridges freeze first; in a slide, ease off, keep straight, wait for grip; in a skid, look and steer where you want to go, then steer back as it straightens; clear every window, light, mirror and plate before you roll.
Glossary: bald tires means heavily worn tires with little tread; traction means the grip between tires and road; hydroplaning means tires sliding on a layer of water; skid means a loss of control as the tires lose grip; ABS means an anti-lock braking system; cruise control means a setting that holds a steady speed automatically; livestock means farm animals such as cattle.
